qualification: Actual native MIDI/XM workers pass full playback and rewind, then first resumed packets differ after nonzero seek despite identical timestamps/lengths. MIDI500ms loses held-note phase/state; XM120ms loses active-sample/tracker history. Both independently reproduce before the fix.

Reader reset hooks reset the synth then decode preceding windows without presenting their PCM, restoring phase/voices/controllers/tracker state before the already selected raw packet. Raw seek landing and next-packet semantics stay unchanged. EOF skips reconstruction; rewind starts from fresh state.

Six recording-worker target checks compare PCM bytes and PTS with continuous native synthesis: MIDI500/1500/2100ms and XM120/240/360ms, including release windows. Play and rewind are repeated controls. No extra preroll audio is queued.

5 MIDI/6 XM reader units,31 worker units, related clock/duration/EOF integrations, fixture reproduction and player build pass. Existing short authored audio is read in place and hashes checked; separate native video control is authored. Ordinary tests need no encoder/network.

History reconstruction is linear in prior rendered timeline and can make long seeks slower; no performance improvement, checkpoints or physical-device claim. It fixes correctness without claiming reference-quality synthesis.
Shared capture assertions now compare packet count/timestamps/PCM with concise diagnostics rather than dumping entire synthetic sample arrays; infrastructure changes count zero.
compatibility: Stateful seek output now matches continuous synthesis while retaining public cursor/PTS and interface signatures. Reset errors propagate through the existing terminal worker path.
counting: One missing synth-state restoration problem across MIDI/XM. Notes, phases, controllers, targets, sample variants and diagnostic changes add no IDs.
